evidence: The comment's blanket claim 'a line that does not match is not silently dropped' was false for non-`- ` lines, so the overclaim was real; the reviewer itself conditioned the code change on whether transport.js emits one line per finding, and the agent answered that flattenBody collapses VERTICAL_SEPARATORS, then scoped the comment instead of adding folding code for an input the producer cannot emit.
guidance_note: When a comment asserts a no-loss guarantee, state the producer invariant it rests on (with its source) in the same comment rather than a blanket claim the parser does not enforce.

evidence: The original body_findings used `r.get("state") == "CHANGES_REQUESTED"` while change_requests used its own `r["state"] == "CHANGES_REQUESTED"`, yet the docstring claimed 'one predicate'; 6ce8e82 extracted is_blocking_review and routed both through it.
guidance_note: When a docstring claims two call sites share one rule, make them call one function before writing the claim.

evidence: Round 1 reviewed a6fae4f at 09:55:47, before 6ce8e82 (fix for F2, pushed ~09:57) landed, so this is F2 re-raised on the pre-fix code and 6ce8e82 indeed resolves it. The ON-POST-REVIEW flag points at a6fae4f, which only changed heading matching; the finding is a duplicate, not caused by that commit.

fetch does add a third bot_reviews read per iteration, but each is one page on a normal PR and paginated only past 100 reviews; the agent declined coupling fetch and change_requests through a shared snapshot and fixed the docstring overclaim instead. The flag's commit a6fae4f only changed heading parsing; the extra read was in the original PR.

The agent argues a truncated body loses its trailing REVIEW_MARKER so head_review_verdict halts before fetch; the packet does not show parse_agent_artifact or whether GitHub truncates rather than rejects an oversized body, so neither the reviewer's risk nor the agent's rebuttal is verifiable here. The flagged commit a6fae4f did not touch this logic.

The original SKILL.md paragraph said both 'that dismissal is what clears it' and 'the re-review on the new head drops it', while body_findings keeps returning the finding while its review stays CHANGES_REQUESTED; 7dad84f made dismissal the sole clearer. The paragraph dates from the original PR, so the a6fae4f flag is a false positive.
guidance_note: After writing the mechanism for a new state, reread every prose sentence that describes how that state clears and check each against the code path that reads it.

evidence: 6ce8e82 (F2's fix) wrote 'the same set by construction' into both docstrings when only the predicate, not the bot_reviews snapshot, was shared, which was a real overclaim; the race itself needs a new CHANGES_REQUESTED review between two adjacent reads with no push, so the agent's docstring-only fix and its refusal to couple the reads hold up.
guidance_note: When extracting a shared predicate, claim only what the extraction shares; 'same set by construction' needs one shared read, not one shared filter.

evidence: 6ce8e82, F1's comment fix, wrote the raw U+2028/U+2029 characters into the comment ('(\n \r    )' in the diff, with visible line breaks in the hunk); a35fa48 replaced them with escaped text. The finding is flagged on 7dad84f but the defect entered in 6ce8e82.
guidance_note: When documenting a character set that includes invisible or line-separator code points, write them as escapes, never as literals pasted from the source.

evidence: SKILL.md step 8 demanded per-review enumeration of body findings while the canonical finding carried no review id, a real contract gap; the agent changed the record to round-level instead of widening the finding shape. The flag is a false positive: 7dad84f touched only docstrings and the step-8 paragraph, not this mismatch, which dates from the original PR.
guidance_note: When a procedure asks the agent to partition data by a key, confirm the data shape carries that key before writing the procedure.

guidance_note: When turning a re-export into a local wrapper, grep the file's comments for that name and update every provenance claim.

evidence: The test cases covered `README.md:211`, `a:b.py:10` and no-code-span lines but no zero-colon span, so `_split_path_line`'s `(span, None)` branch was untested; 1a541a2 added the case. a35fa48, the flagged commit, changed only comments, so the flag is a false positive.
guidance_note: Write one test per branch of a new parser helper, including the nullable-field shape the contract documents.

narrative: The PR added out-of-diff body-finding parsing to address-pr-reviews and ran into the reviewer's 5-round cap. Round 2 existed only because F2's fix wrote a 'same set by construction' docstring that overclaimed what was shared (F7). F1's comment fix also pasted raw U+2028/U+2029 characters, which round 3 caught (F8); that round also had the original-PR findings F9 and F10. Pushbacks on perf (F4) and the race refactor (F7) were sound; the truncation rebuttal (F5) cannot be checked from the packet.
guidance_observations: Fix commits that rewrite docstrings introduced two of the later findings, so a fix's new prose needs the same check against the code as its new code.
Round 1 re-raised F2 because the review ran before the fix was pushed; batching plan replies and pushes sooner shortens that window.
The review hit MAX_REVIEW_ROUNDS, so the final commit 1a541a2 stands unreviewed by the bot.

evidence: 7a4cf65 widened the guard to cover the transcript read and the verdict but left the `hook_event_name` sys.exit outside it, a pre-gate exit with no log line; cb5979e moved it inside. 7a4cf65 was a self-initiated post-review commit with no reviewer finding in this packet, so there is no finding id to name, though this is the remainder of that commit's incomplete sweep.
guidance_note: When the rule is 'every exit before the gate leaves a record', list every exit between stdin and the gate and put each inside the guard in the same commit.

evidence: 7a4cf65 added a no-transcript_path test that writes the same isolated log before the no-cwd test, making that test's comment 'Nothing else writes this log' false; cb5979e reworded both comments. The drift came from self-initiated commit 7a4cf65, not from any reviewer finding in the packet, so caused_by is null.
guidance_note: When inserting a test that writes shared fixture state, reread the comments of the tests after it that describe that state.

evidence: F1's fix (cb5979e) wrote 'every way the hook can stop before it gates' while deliberately leaving json.load outside the guard ('an unparseable payload has no dict to log against'); a non-dict payload then raised TypeError inside the guard, and log()'s hook.get raised AttributeError, losing the record. eaa5a0b moved the parse inside and handled non-dicts.
guidance_note: Before claiming a guard covers every failure, run it against malformed inputs at the boundary (non-JSON, null, a scalar, a list) and check the handler's own dependencies on the input's shape.

evidence: Once 7a4cf65 moved stop() inside the guard, a failure after resolve_ceiling succeeded was logged as `ceiling=unresolved`; eaa5a0b initialized ceiling before the try, as tokens already was. The cause is self-initiated commit 7a4cf65, not a reviewer finding, and the cb5979e flag did not change this, so caused_by is null.
guidance_note: When widening a try block, track every value the except handler logs with an initial sentinel, the same way the first one was tracked.

narrative: The bot approved the original change twice. The agent then pushed 7a4cf65, a self-initiated widening of the log-on-stop guard, and every later finding traces to it being incomplete. It left the event check outside (F1), staled a test comment (F2), and logged a resolved ceiling as unresolved (F4). F1's fix again stopped short at json.load (F3). Every reviewer premise was correct and every acceptance was right.
guidance_observations: The scope grew in steps (config, then payload keys, then the event check, then stdin shape), and each step cost a review round. Enumerating every pre-gate exit once would have closed it in one commit.
The agent's F1 reply stated why json.load stayed outside, and the next round showed that reasoning was wrong; a stated exclusion needs testing against malformed input, not just an argument.

evidence: The window is real (old SHARED_AT_START, a first CONFIG_NAME still staged as a partial, a concurrent sweep), but it needs a session unseen for 30 days plus a sweep at that instant, and the result is a loud, retryable `ceiling` error, so S4 overstates it. 7e05a2e later documented exactly this as accepted, but the thread got no reply and stayed unresolved. The 652706f flag is a false positive: that commit added only a docstring and a test, and _last_seen's logic predates it.
guidance_note: When adding a deleter to a directory other writers use, list each writer's write window in the original PR and state which races are accepted.

evidence: The original sweep caught every OSError, including FileNotFoundError from a lost concurrent rmtree, and printed 'cannot sweep'; by 27f3989 a dedicated `except FileNotFoundError: pass` arm exists, so the agent fixed it without replying on the thread. The sweep loop predates the flagged commit 652706f.
guidance_note: When a best-effort delete can race a peer doing the same delete, treat 'already gone' as success when first writing the except arms.

evidence: lines_in's exists-then-read_text pattern only caught UnicodeDecodeError, so a sweep removing a live reader's file mid-read crashed the Stop hook. F5's text confirms the read-side race was later 'explicitly called out and handled in lines_in's docstring and the FileNotFoundError catch', but the thread got no reply. This was a gap in the original sweep, not in 652706f.
guidance_note: When introducing a deleter, grep for every reader of the paths it removes and make each tolerate the file vanishing between check and read.

evidence: The reviewer quotes README.md 'Nothing removes that record', which the sweep makes false; the round 5 summary shows a second top-level file now in the diff, consistent with a README fix, but the packet does not show it and the thread got no reply. This was stale in the original PR.
guidance_note: When a change reverses a documented guarantee, grep the README for the guarantee's wording in the same commit.

evidence: The fix for F3 hardened only the read side, and F5 points at the matching write-side window; it also restates F1's unanswered ceiling-write race. Its claim that mark_seen's os.utime fails unhandled is wrong, since mark_seen catches OSError (per the hunk and 7e05a2e). 7e05a2e answered by documenting the window as accepted, still with no thread reply.
guidance_note: When fixing one side of a race a new deleter opens, sweep its mirror (readers and writers) in the same fix, and answer the earlier thread that raised it.

evidence: The fix for F3 added a `_VanishedMidRead` test that calls lines_in directly, contradicting the section header 'never off the internals'. The flagged commit 7e05a2e is docstring-only; the drift came from the F3 fix commit, which the packet does not show. Round 7 approved, which implies a fix, but the thread got no reply.
guidance_note: When adding a test that breaks a section header's stated rule, edit the header in the same commit.

narrative: The PR added a 30-day sweep of the sessions tree. Round 3 raised four real gaps in the original sweep: a staging race, the lost-race log noise, a reader TOCTOU, and the stale README. The agent fixed most of them in code but posted no reply on any thread and left all six unresolved. The F3 fix covered only the read side, so round 5 raised the write-side mirror (F5); its new test contradicted the section header, which round 6 raised (F6). Three runs were cancelled by newer pushes.
guidance_observations: The agent fixed findings without replying or resolving threads, so the audit trail address-pr-reviews requires is missing and the dispositions are only inferable from later commits.
Three review runs were cancelled when a newer push arrived; batching fixes into one push per round would have saved those runs' tokens.

evidence: The token-drop test 'tokens < frozen_at' cannot tell an auto-compaction from a landed /clear. The agent's own medium-review issue comment agrees ('compaction confounds the token-drop heuristic') and limits the marker to one stop, filing promptctl-context-ceiling-yr8 for an authoritative landing signal. The inline thread itself got no reply and stayed unresolved.
guidance_note: When inferring an event from a proxy signal, list the other events that move the same signal before shipping the inference.

narrative: The PR re-derives a reset-in-place session's shared record when the context shrinks below the close-out size. Round 0 was cancelled. Round 1 raised one real finding: auto-compaction confounds the token-drop proxy. The agent narrowed the marker's lifetime to one stop, filed the authoritative fix as a ticket, and round 2 approved. The thread was never answered inline; the disposition lives only in an issue comment.
guidance_observations: Dispositions were posted as PR issue comments for the local review passes while the bot's inline thread was left unanswered and unresolved.
